subject: Dedicated reservation options & ramp proposal for Cortex Labs
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cortex-labs.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — Q4 go-live planning

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Cortex is moving toward a Q4 pilot (internal goal: early Nov) for our pharmacophore inference service. We expect a bursty inference workload driven by nightly batch rescoring plus 24/7 low-latency API traffic. High-level numbers from our side:
- Target concurrent active sessions: ~180–220
- Average response size: ~700–900 tokens
- Expected sustained requests-per-second (p95): 45–60
- Peak short bursts: up to ~350 RPS for a few hours

We want a proposal that includes: 1) dedicated cluster sizing options (min GPUs reserved, recommended cluster), 2) ramp schedule (how to get from pilot to full), 3) pricing for reserved vs. burst capacity, and 4) any constraints around model variants / quantization you recommend.

Also include SOC2 evidence and network peering / VPC details for procurement. Can you get something over by early next week? Procurement will need it.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Infrastructure, Cortex Labs
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cortex-labs.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-02T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Q4 go-live planning

Alyssa —

Appreciate the clear numbers. Attached is an initial options pack (CL-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf) with three reservation profiles and a recommended ramp. High level summary here so procurement has a readable option list up front:

Option Small (pilot-friendly) — Recommended for proof-of-concept- Reserved: 8 x A100 80GB GPUs (min reserved)- Typical concurrency target: ~40–60 active sessions- Expected sustained throughput: ~15–25 RPS (depending on model size/quant)- Ramp: immediate for pilot (Week 0–4), scale to 25% of projected full by month 2- Price: reserved baseline + usage-burst at 1.8x reserved rate

Option Medium — Balanced for pilot→prod transition (recommended starting point)- Reserved: 24 x A100 80GB GPUs (min reserved)- Baseline sustained throughput: ~55–120 RPS- Concurrency headroom for model variants / KV cache warmup- Ramp: M1 30% capacity, M3 60%, M6 full- Price: lower per-GPU reserved rate; burst pricing tiers included

Option Large — Enterprise steady-state- Reserved: 64 x H100-equivalent GPUs (combination H100/A100 as available)- Engineered for sustained high throughput and lower p99 latency- Ramp: canary week, then M1 50%, M2 75%, M4 full- Price: deepest discount for 12+ month commit

Operational notes:
- Minimum reservation is configurable; we can split the reservation across two AZs for redundancy.
- We include automatic prefix/KV caching and an initial cache-warm plan to reduce early token cost.
- Burst capacity is available but subject to regional capacity; we recommend a 10–15% buffer in committed GPUs or a small burst pool.
- We recommend H100 for lowest latency if your model variants are latency-sensitive; otherwise A100 80GB is cost-effective.

I attached a one-page ramp diagram and cost examples. Next steps: 1) confirm a preferred option and target go-live week, 2) procurement sends PO template, 3) we finalize SOW & legal (I’ll loop in finance/legal).

I'll also attach SOC2 artifacts and VPC peering docs in the next message for procurement.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-02T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Dedicated reservation options & ramp proposal for Cortex Labs

Rachel / team —

Quick internal notes on the attached options (high-level):
- If they truly need sub-100ms p99 for short queries, we should push H100s in the Medium option and tighten canary (3-day golden traffic) before full ramp.
- For the Medium option, consider proposing a min-reserve of 18 GPUs (instead of 24) with an explicit burst SLA that guarantees access to +6 GPUs within 48 hrs — gives them lower up-front commit while we hold a burst pool.
- Add explicit TTL and sizing for KV cache to the SOW (affects host mem footprint and kernel selection).
- Suggest a pre-warm / pre-provisioning fee for rapid scale (if they want full capacity within 2–3 weeks). That protects other regional commitments.

I can give a quick kernel/quant guidance bullet list for the SOC2 and ops appendix if you want to include it.

Jonas
Director, Solutions Engineering
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Dedicated reservation options & ramp proposal for Cortex Labs

Looping in pricing:
- If Cortex commits 12 months on the Medium profile (24 GPU equivalent), we can do 15% off list for reserved GPUs and remove the pre-warm fee.
- If they commit only 6 months, discount drops to 7% and pre-warm fee applies.
- For the 18 GPU min variant (jonas's suggestion), discount targets are 10% (12mo) / 5% (6mo).
- Approvals: I need written approval from Sales leadership for anything below 12% discount on a 12-month case.

Also confirm that we can include a one-time migration credits bucket for up to 100k tokens to help the pilot.

Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cortex-labs.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-06T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Dedicated reservation options & ramp proposal for Cortex Labs

Rachel —

Thanks for the options. Cortex prefers the Medium profile but we'd like to negotiate the following:
1) Minimum reserve reduced to 18 GPUs (to help manage headcount in Q3).
2) Ramp accelerated: pilot → 50% by week 6 and full capacity by month 3 (we can invest in cache-warm tooling on our side).
3) Can you confirm burst access: guaranteed +6 GPUs within 48 hours (we need this in writing for our ops team)?
4) Procurement attached a PO template (PO-template_Cortex.pdf). We also need SOC2 report, peering runbook, and a short note on where model quantization will affect latency/throughput.

If you can amend the Medium option with the 18-GPU min and the expedited ramp, we can move forward and send a PO.

Regards,
Alyssa
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@cortex-labs.com>, eng-procurement@cortex-labs.com

Alyssa —

Thanks — we can accommodate the Medium profile variant with your requested changes. Summary of updates (attached as CL-dedicated-proposal-v3.pdf and SOW-draft.docx):
- Medium (variant): Reserved min 18 x A100 80GB GPUs (will be delivered as a mix of A100/H100 where available).
- Accelerated ramp: pilot → 50% by end of week 6; full capacity by month 3 (we'll run a 7-day canary with your traffic ahead of each step).
- Burst pool guarantee: Redwood will commit to making +6 GPUs available within 48 hours via our regional burst buffer; formal SLA language included in the SOW appendix.
- Pricing: 10% discount on reserved GPUs for a 12-month commitment on the 18-GPU variant (Marissa: this aligns with the mid-tier discount band).
- SOC2 + peering: SOC2 Type II artifact and VPC peering runbook attached. Jonas included a short quant/kernel note in the ops appendix.

Next steps:
1) Procurement to send signed PO (we received PO-template_Cortex.pdf) — we'll draft the final SOW once the PO is in.
2) Legal to review (I’ll kick off with Legal & copy you on DocuSign).
3) Scheduling: once PO is accepted, we will pre-provision the 18 GPUs and open the canary window within 5 business days.

I've attached the updated proposal and SOW draft as requested. Let me know if you want a short call to go through the ramp milestones.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference
